title: Straitline Systems — Platform Activation: Pilot Scope & Security Handover
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week pilot to validate Redwood hosted inference for Straitline's customer chat & content summarization workloads. Covered scope, success criteria, security checklist (SOC2, KMS integration, VPC peering), basic runbook and initial SLA expectations. Agreed to run a 48-hour latency/cost benchmark and share pricing + pilot SOW.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Evan, Rosa - Redwood; Priya, Liam, Sara, Noah - Straitline

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro round, im Maya Thompson, your AE. Evan is our SE, Rosa from CS.
[00:10] Priya: Hi all, Priya here. Couple minutes from us, Liam will drive the engineering parts, Sara will take security questions.
[00:18] Evan: Cool, thanks. High level agenda: scope pilot, map success criteria, security checklist, then operational next steps.
[00:30] Liam: Weve been running a small proof-of-concept on open-model endpoints, but throughput is the pain point. Need to see cost per 1M tokens and p95 latency at our expected qps.
[00:45] Rosa: Great context. For the pilot we usually recommend a 4-6 week window with two phases: ingest & smoke tests, then a load/benchmark phase.
[01:05] Sara: On security: we are SOC2 in progress, need audit logs, KMS integration, and bring-your-own-key support ideally. Also data residency, logs retention.
[01:20] Evan: Absolutely. Our private/Dedicated options provide VPC peering or Dedicated capacity; hosted has encryption-in-transit plus optional customer-managed KMS via our private offering. For the pilot we can run hosted with VPC peering and KMS integration for key wrapping — depends on your timeline.
[01:40] Noah: Timeline: we need to show infra-level performance within 6 weeks, stakeholder review on Sept 30th. Also procurement wants a short SOW.
[01:50] Maya: Noted. Let's walk through explicit success criteria so we can size the pilot and present to procurement.
[02:05] Priya: Success criteria: 1) p95 latency <= 250ms for single-turn queries up to 512 tokens, 2) cost no more than our current baseline per 1M tokens, 3) no PII leakage and logs aligned with our retention policy.
[02:25] Evan: Ok p95 250ms is achievable on Dedicated for that seq length, hosted maybe if we tune batching and KV cache. We'll capture representative prompt samples and token distributions.
[02:45] Liam: We do a lot of short queries and some long-form summarization. Throughput will spike during daily digest jobs so burst capacity is important. How do you handle autoscale?
[03:00] Evan: For dedicated pools you get autoscale policies, burst nodes; hosted can route to a higher tier model variant as fallback. We'll include a config for autoscale thresholds in the runbook.
[03:15] Sara: KMS details: can we use our cloud KMS, and will keys ever land on Redwood-managed HSM? We need a model where we control key rotation and have key material never exported.
[03:30] Evan: Yes, BYOK via your cloud KMS is supported in our Private deployment and in Dedicated with a customer-managed KMS integration. Keys are used for envelope encryption; Redwood does not export your raw key material. For hosted we can offer a managed wrapper but you'd need Dedicated/Private for strict BYOK guarantees.
[03:50] Priya: That may push us to Dedicated but we need proof the latency/cost tradeoff is worth it. Can you run a 48-hour benchmark mimicking our traffic?
[04:05] Maya: We can. Typical approach: you send a tokenized workload sample, we run a staged benchmark — first smoke, then load at your qps with representative bursts, capture p50/p95/p99, and cost metrics.
[04:25] Liam: We'll share a payload set and the s3 link by EOD tomorrow. Include the summarization prompts and chat patterns.
[04:35] Rosa: Good. On observability: Console will show per-route latency/cost, token-level breakdown, and logs. We can give Rosa map of the dashboard and tracing hooks.
[04:50] Noah: Networking: we prefer VPC peering over public endpoints. Can you confirm support for VPC peering and egress rules?
[05:05] Evan: Yes VPC peering is supported; we'll need CIDR allowances and a staging peering first. For the pilot we usually do a staging peering and then prod peering if tests pass.
[05:20] Sara: Audit logs—what's retained and can we push to our SIEM?
[05:30] Evan: Audit logs include request metadata and model variant used; retention can be configured and we support pushing logs to your SIEM via forwarder. For full request content we can redact PII or disable retention depending on compliance needs.
[05:50] Priya: Great. Can you also detail the fallback behavior for model regressions? We want canary rollouts and automatic fallback if quality regresses.
[06:05] Evan: Rollouts: we support canary percent traffic, A/B splits, and automatic fallback to previous model variant on error rate or quality regression tied to your evals. We'll include this in the rollout policy section of the SOW.
[06:25] Liam: About caching — prefix/KV cache: does Redwood persist KV cache across sessions or is it per request?
[06:38] Evan: KV cache is per model session; we also support prefix caching and a shared cache layer for certain workloads to reduce re-computation. We'll tunable TTLs.
[06:55] Rosa: I'll hand over the pilot runbook template after this meeting. It includes environment checklist, SSH/key handoff, and latency/cost dashboards.
[07:10] Priya: Procurement will need pricing ranges and a skeleton SOW.
[07:20] Maya: We'll send pricing bands — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and a draft 6-week SOW by Wednesday.
[07:30] Noah: Also, we have a mandate to avoid public cloud egress in some regs; how strict is that for hosted?
[07:40] Evan: Hosted routes through our managed infra; for strict egress/no export requirements you'd need Private on-prem or a VPC-only Dedicated setup. We'll call that out in the SOW.
[07:55] Sara: One more on encryption at rest for model cache: need to confirm that local caches are encrypted and keys are managed as described.
[08:05] Evan: Affirmative. We'll include the technical note on disk-level encryption and KMS integration.
[08:20] Priya: Ok, let's align timeline: we aim to start the pilot next Monday, run 4 weeks of testing and 2 weeks of review, stakeholder review 30 Sept.
[08:35] Maya: Sounds good. Quick risk callouts: 1) If p95 target cannot be met on hosted we'll propose Dedicated backbone and estimate delta cost, 2) procurement timeline could push pilot start — need SOW to expedite.
[08:55] Liam: For the benchmark, we also need tokenized cost per model variant, and a breakdown of GPU type used in Dedicated.
[09:10] Evan: We'll include GPU SKUs and perf profile for the model variants we test. Also quantization notes if relevant.
[09:25] Rosa: I'll set up a shared drive with the runbook, sample prompts, and the authentication checklist; invite list includes all present.
[09:35] Priya: Thanks. Any competitors we should be aware of? We're simultaneously evaluating two other vendors.
[09:45] Maya: Understood. Many customers compare to other hosted vendors and some self-hosted runtimes; we'll include a short comparative note.
[09:55] Priya: Perfect.
[10:00] Maya: Ok recap and next steps...

Recap: agree to pilot start next Monday contingent on procurement; strike 48-hour benchmark after Straitline uploads sample workload; Redwood to send pricing bands and draft SOW by Wednesday; Rosa to share runbook and invite; SE to document KMS/VPC specifics and GPU SKU mapping.

End of transcript.
